title: AXI Signoff Evidence Board
description: Select a review area to see which independent assertion, scoreboard, coverage, configuration, or performance artifact should justify signoff.

signals.name: Reset and channel restart
signals.expansion: VALID reset requirements and clean recovery
signals.description: Verify required VALID outputs are LOW during reset and that no monitor invents a transfer until a post-reset VALID/READY handshake occurs.
signals.direction: Reset source and every AXI interface
signals.sampled: Reset assertion, synchronous deassertion, first channel handshakes
signals.verificationNote: Retain traces for reset during idle, backpressure, outstanding reads, and outstanding writes, with recovery behavior tied to the product contract.

signals.name: Channel handshake safety
signals.expansion: VALID independence and stable stalled payload
signals.description: Prove all five source VALID signals are independent of READY and all payload fields remain stable through stalls.
signals.verificationNote: Review every payload member and the no-combinational-path rule; a green VALID-only property is incomplete evidence.

signals.name: Burst and byte-lane legality
signals.expansion: Length, size, type, boundary, LAST, and strobes
signals.description: Demonstrate correct address generation and data-lane ownership for aligned/unaligned FIXED, INCR, and WRAP bursts, including errors and the 4 KB boundary.
signals.sampled: Accepted AW/AR and every accepted W/R beat
signals.typicalUse: Protocol checker, predictor, and crossed coverage
signals.verificationNote: Tie every coverage hit to an assertion/scoreboard pass. Exercise first, middle, and final read errors without canceling the declared beat count.

signals.name: ID and ordering
signals.expansion: Outstanding match and per-ID response queues
signals.description: Show correct response routing, different-ID completion freedom, and same-ID response order for repeated outstanding requests.
signals.sampled: Accepted requests, response beats, B completion, and RLAST
signals.verificationNote: Expected and actual logic must be independent. Track full transaction context; ID selects the ordering stream but is not the expected address or data itself.

signals.name: Outstanding capacity
signals.description: Reach every supported read/write outstanding depth while independently stalling address, data, and response channels.
signals.sampled: Allocation, full, simultaneous retire/allocate, and drain
signals.verificationNote: Force same-ID and different-ID occupancy, route contention, and response backpressure; average random traffic rarely sustains the exact boundary state.

signals.name: Errors and optional features
signals.expansion: Response semantics, exclusives, and configured attributes
signals.description: Align checker behavior with the implemented AXI revision, optional signals, exclusive support, user fields, and documented error/timeout policy.
signals.verificationNote: Do not treat EXOKAY as a generic success or an absent optional signal as zero without checking the specification's default/interoperability rules.

signals.name: Coverage closure
signals.expansion: Legal holes, conditional bins, and exclusions
signals.description: Review each legal hole and conditional combination against the verification plan, with reproducible tests and justified exclusions.
signals.sampled: After stable assertion and scoreboard results
signals.verificationNote: A response-by-burst cross cannot alone decide exclusive legality because AxLOCK and exclusive restrictions are additional dimensions.

signals.name: Progress and performance
signals.description: Validate configured latency, service, throughput, and starvation-prevention requirements under realistic contention and backpressure assumptions.
signals.direction: System contract → performance monitors and liveness proofs
signals.verificationNote: Separate protocol compliance from a product performance promise. Record the QoS policy, arbitration assumptions, traffic envelope, and proof bound.
